title: Popeyes U.S. comps fall 5.2% in Q2 2026 — a sixth straight negative quarter
means: The decline moderated from -6.5% in Q1, which management will present as progress. It isn't recovery. Six consecutive negative quarters at ~$235K of restaurant-level profit is a franchisee solvency timeline, not a marketing problem — and the Sailormen bankruptcy already showed what the end of that timeline looks like.

title: Wingstop domestic same-store sales drop 7.5%; full-year guidance cut to -4% to -6%
means: Wingstop opened 102 restaurants in the same quarter its comps fell 7.5%. That is the definition of a development machine outrunning its demand curve. With AUV already down from $2.1M to $2.0M, every new urban unit is now splitting a shrinking digital order base — and franchisee-credit Wingstop net-lease product should be underwritten on that math, not on WING's balance sheet.

title: KFC has closed more than 300 U.S. restaurants in twelve months
means: 312 closures between July 2025 and July 2026 — 7.64% of the American footprint. Read it as inventory, not obituary: three hundred freestanding, drive-thru-equipped boxes in trade areas that have supported chicken for decades just came back to the market, most of them controlled by legacy franchisees with no interest in redevelopment.

title: New-construction Chick-fil-A ground lease trades at a 4.15% cap — a Tennessee record
means: $2.77M for a 6,008 SF relocation store on 1.74 acres in Hixson, on a 15-year corporate absolute-NNN ground lease with 10% bumps. The lowest cap rate ever recorded for a single-tenant Chick-fil-A drive-thru in Tennessee, per CoStar — and it was achieved on a shorter-than-standard term. Chick-fil-A ground leases are now priced closer to bonds than to restaurants.

title: Net lease cap rates tick up: corporate QSR 5.85%, franchisee QSR 6.85%
means: The 100 basis point spread between corporate and franchisee QSR is the single most important number in chicken real estate. It is the market pricing exactly what CSW tracks: who actually operates the restaurant. In a year with a major Popeyes franchisee bankruptcy, expect that spread to widen — and to widen most for brands with negative comps.

title: Zaxby's opens its first New York City restaurant in the Bronx
means: A Southeast chicken brand with a 3,500 SF suburban dine-in DNA is now operating in the Bronx, with a 2,800 SF, 16-seat Upper East Side unit behind it. If the small-format Northeast box clears anywhere near the $2.71M system AUV, Zaxby's franchise recruiting stops being a regional pitch.

title: KFC leans into boneless chicken, wings and sauces as U.S. comps turn positive
means: Three consecutive quarters of positive comps after seven negative ones, on the back of spicy wings and returning potato wedges. KFC is finally competing on the parts of the bird the market actually wants instead of defending the bucket. The turnaround is real — it is just happening across 3,523 restaurants instead of 3,669.

title: Houston TX Hot Chicken enters the UK through a PizzaExpress franchise agreement
means: Three UK locations in 2026 and 50 over three years — but the structure is the story. Partnering with an established operator platform rather than recruiting franchisees is how a 25-unit American brand gets international scale without international infrastructure.

title: Multi-Brand 50: KBP Brands reaches 1,224 units and 831 KFCs
means: One operator controls roughly a quarter of the U.S. KFC system while the brand closes 300 restaurants a year. KBP is simultaneously the largest buyer and the largest potential seller in KFC real estate — and it has already diversified into Arby's and Sonic, which tells you how it reads the brand's long-term U.S. trajectory.

title: Bankrupt Popeyes franchisee Sailormen sells 97 restaurants for $16.55M to five buyers
means: Read the per-store prices: Popeyes corporate paid $600K per restaurant for 16 Miami units; 61 Biscuits paid $370K per restaurant in West Palm Beach; Pulse paid about $54K per restaurant for 50 units across Tampa, Tallahassee, Pensacola and Jacksonville. That spread is a live map of where Popeyes trade areas still work and where they don't. Thirty-three restaurants found no buyer at all and went dark through lease rejection.

title: Dave's Hot Chicken opens eight restaurants in a single day
means: With 150+ openings planned for 2026 and roughly 1,000 units in development, Dave's is consuming drive-thru pad sites faster than any brand in the category. It is now the marginal bidder on a large share of American QSR real estate — and the reason second-generation chicken boxes are clearing quickly.

title: Raising Cane's opens its 1,000th restaurant on Hollywood Boulevard
means: A thousand restaurants, virtually all company-operated, at a $6.3M AUV. There is no franchisee base to consolidate, no operator distress to trade, and no franchise transfers to broker — Cane's growth creates real estate opportunity only at the site-selection and sale-leaseback stage. Get in early or don't get in.

title: El Pollo Loco closes fiscal 2025 at $1.13B in system-wide sales
means: Flat full-year comps (+0.1%) with a Q4 acceleration to +2.1% and a 17.8% restaurant contribution margin. Healthy unit economics, minimal unit growth — nine openings against a 500-restaurant base. LOCO is a margin story, not a development story.

title: Wingstop closes fiscal 2025 with 3,056 restaurants and $5.3B in system-wide sales
means: 493 net new units, 19.2% unit growth, 12.1% systemwide sales growth — and AUV down to $2.0M. The 2025 report contained the warning that the 2026 comps confirmed: system sales were growing on unit count, not on restaurant-level demand.

title: RBI: Popeyes U.S. comps -3.2% for 2025; franchisee profitability falls to ~$235,000
means: The $235K figure is the most consequential number RBI disclosed. At that level, a franchisee carrying acquisition debt across 100 units cannot service it. Sailormen filed in January. Assume more filings follow before comps turn.

title: Zaxby's surpasses 1,000 locations
means: From 969 units at the end of 2024 to more than 1,000, with a projected $2.8B in system sales and a $2.71M AUV — the third-highest unit volume in the category behind Chick-fil-A and Cane's. Zaxby's has quietly become the strongest franchised chicken investment outside the top two.

title: Sailormen, one of Popeyes' largest franchisees, files Chapter 11 with 136 restaurants
means: 3,300 employees, $233.5M of fiscal 2025 revenue, 136 restaurants across Florida and Georgia — gone as a going concern within twelve months of the franchisor reporting $235K average restaurant profit. The largest single distress event in chicken franchising this cycle.

title: Korpal Group signs a 13-unit Golden Chick development agreement for Houston and Beaumont
means: Ten Houston units over four years and three in Beaumont over ten. Second-generation Subway operators redeploying family capital into a higher-AUV chicken concept is the single most common pattern in Texas chicken development right now — and it means ten Houston sites need to be found, entitled and built by an operator who does not yet control them.

title: Wholesale wings close 2025 at $0.98/lb, roughly half the prior year's $1.88
means: Boneless skinless breast also fell to $1.16/lb from a mid-year peak of $2.77. Cheap wings are a margin windfall for Wingstop franchisees at exactly the moment their traffic is falling — which is why Wingstop's Q2 2026 net income rose 16.9% while same-store sales fell 7.5%. Commodity relief is masking demand deterioration across the category.

title: Layne's Chicken Fingers doubles its footprint to 40 units and adds 10 new franchisees
means: 21 openings in one year, 68 restaurants under signed agreements including a single 44-store Texas deal, and franchisees arriving from Wendy's and Arby's systems. When experienced multi-unit operators underwrite a 40-unit brand, they are buying prototype economics, not brand equity.

title: Slim Chickens signs 110 development agreements in 2025; pipeline passes 1,200 restaurants
means: A 4:1 ratio of committed pipeline to open restaurants is the highest in the category. It is also the number most likely to be discounted — signed area development agreements convert at well under 100%. Hiring a former Starbucks site-strategy executive as CDO says leadership knows the constraint is real estate throughput, not demand.

title: Chick-fil-A systemwide sales approach $24 billion on a $9.16M average unit volume
means: $23.9B, +5.2%, on 2,863 outlets plus 435 licensed venues. Six operating days a week. The growth came from 179 new restaurants rather than same-store volume, which is why the $1B international commitment and the licensed channel are now the strategic priorities — the domestic drive-thru is running out of hours in the day.

title: Church's Texas Chicken adds units and lifts AUV to $1.138M
means: 885 U.S. stores entering 2026 and a third straight year of AUV growth off a ~$1.0M base. Church's has stopped shrinking. It remains the lowest-volume national chicken brand by a wide margin, which caps what any Church's site can pay in rent — underwrite accordingly.

title: Church's plots a 600-unit China expansion under the Texas Chicken brand
means: The U.S. system grew by 12 units in 2025. The international pipeline is measured in hundreds. For a value-positioned brand with a $1.1M domestic AUV, that allocation of ambition is entirely rational — and it tells U.S. franchisees where the franchisor's attention is going.

title: Golden Chick opens its 250th restaurant after a record 23 openings in 2025
means: A 60-year-old Texas brand having its best development year ever, with entries planned for Nevada, Arkansas, Missouri and Arizona. Golden Chick's growth is concentrated in a handful of operator families — SXThree alone is targeting 100 units by 2030 — which makes the operator list, not the brand, the real pipeline.

title: Technomic: chicken chain sales growth slows to 5.3% in 2025
means: Down from 9.1% in 2024 and more than 12% in 2023 — still comfortably ahead of the 3% industry, but the era of automatic double-digit chicken growth is over. Category-wide, growth is now being redistributed rather than created: Dave's, Cane's and Zaxby's are taking it out of KFC, Popeyes and Jollibee.

title: USDA: per-capita chicken availability hits a record 102.8 lbs in 2026
means: Chicken remains the most consumed animal protein in the United States and is still growing. The demand backdrop is not the problem for Popeyes, KFC or Wingstop. Share is.

title: Jollibee closes 200+ stores in the first half of 2026 and cuts its opening target
means: The group trimmed 2026 openings to 1,000–1,100 from 1,200–1,300. When an aggressive international operator pulls in its development horns, it is usually reading consumer softness ahead of the domestic brands.

title: Four Corners Property Trust acquires 33 properties for $85.5M in the first half of 2026
means: FCPT is the most visible institutional buyer in restaurant net lease and has bought Popeyes assets with ~20 years of term. Its acquisition pace is a useful proxy for where institutional capital thinks restaurant real estate is priced correctly — and its 2026 buying has skewed heavily toward non-restaurant service retail.

title: Roark Capital acquires a majority stake in Dave's Hot Chicken at a $1B valuation
means: A 245-unit brand valued at $1B — roughly $4M per restaurant, against domestic systemwide sales of $617M. Roark underwrote the development pipeline, not the current cash flow. Everything Dave's has done since (150+ openings in 2026, eight in a single day, ~1,000 in development) is that thesis being executed.

title: Hooters sells all 151 company restaurants to franchisee groups in Chapter 11
means: Filed with $376M of debt, closed roughly 30 restaurants in a single day, and emerged as a fully franchisee-owned system. The operating brand survives; what hit the market was a batch of 4,500–6,500 SF casual-dining pads that will not re-tenant as chicken. They re-tenant as something bigger.

title: Eyas Capital acquires BOJ of WNC — Bojangles' largest franchisee, 120 units in six states
means: Jeff Rigsby went from six Asheville restaurants in 2001 to the brand's largest franchisee, then sold to an investment platform that immediately committed to 40+ new units in Ohio. Bojangles' unit count did not move. Ownership of 120 restaurants did. That is exactly the transaction that brand-level data will never show you.

title: KFC moves its U.S. headquarters from Louisville to Plano, Texas
means: Roughly 100 corporate roles relocating over six months, 90 remote roles over 18. Symbolically, the brand most identified with a single American state left it. Practically, it consolidates KFC U.S. alongside KFC Global and Pizza Hut Global in Plano — and puts the U.S. team in the same metro as a large share of its franchisee base.
